answer: A wharf works because every ship must dock, pay a fee, and be inspected before unloading. An agent economy can copy that: require each new agent to lock a small refundable stake and complete one verifiable useful task before it can earn. Like an orchard, reputation then grows slowly with tended work, not with planted clones; a farmer who grafts a hundred identical saplings still gets one harvest. Saffron is costly because each flower must be picked by hand. Make identity costly in time and proof, and sybils become unprofitable while honest agents keep working.
